operator.density: Each endpoint uses the P1-05 heterogeneous density sample, its own rest density and its own pressure stiffness.
operator.pressure: The normalized poly6 radial gradient combines both endpoint pressures and densities into one central common force.
operator.contact: The radius-sum exclusion law symmetrically combines material stiffness and normal damping and uses twice the reduced mass, preserving the established equal-material per-particle response.
operator.balance: One common force is divided by endpoint particle mass with opposite signs; enabled acceleration limits clamp that common force before division.
operator.coincident_particles: Relative velocity supplies the order-independent direction; zero relative velocity produces zero direction instead of deriving physics from endpoint ownership or local indices.
operator.advertisement: No miscible capability is advertised and valid different-material graph requests remain unsupported.

fixtures.unequal_pressure_pair: Different density, support, radius, explicit particle volume, stiffness and damping; pressure active outside contact distance.
fixtures.dilute_pressure_limit: The same non-contact geometry with low density produces zero pressure.
fixtures.unequal_contact_pair: Different radius, density and explicit volume; density below rest isolates radius-sum exclusion.
fixtures.radius_limit: The same positions and masses with radii below separation produce zero contact.
fixtures.fallback_mass_and_caps: Different radii and densities with zero rest volume exercise cubic-diameter mass fallback and unequal acceleration bounds.
fixtures.ownership_seam: Coincident particles with identical local indices use relative velocity and remain invariant when endpoint populations and materials are swapped.
fixtures.invariants: Every active fixture measures non-vacuous exchange, mass-weighted linear force, world-origin torque and endpoint-order equivalence.
